questions.q: ΔABC is inscribed in a circle with Centre O. If AB = 21 cm, BC = 20 cm and AC = 29 cm, then what is the length of the circumradius of the triangle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Check for a Pythagorean triplet: 20² + 21² = 400 + 441 = 841, and 29² = 841.

Since AB² + BC² = AC², ΔABC is a right-angled triangle.

The circumcentre of a right-angled triangle always lies exactly at the midpoint of its hypotenuse.

⇒ Circumradius = Hypotenuse ÷ 2

⇒ Circumradius = 29 ÷ 2 = 14.5 cm

∴ The correct answer is 14.5 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

In ΔABC:

⇒ AB = 21 cm, BC = 20 cm, and AC = 29 cm

Formula Used:

⇒ Circumradius (R) = (a × b × c) ÷ (4 × Area)

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

⇒ Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)]

Calculations:

First, find the semi-perimeter (s) of the triangle:

⇒ s = (21 + 20 + 29) ÷ 2 = 70 ÷ 2 = 35 cm

Calculate the area using Heron's formula:

⇒ Area = √[35 × (35 − 21) × (35 − 20) × (35 − 29)]

⇒ Area = √[35 × 14 × 15 × 6]

⇒ Area = √44100 = 210 cm²

Substitute the values into the circumradius formula:

⇒ R = (21 × 20 × 29) ÷ (4 × 210)

⇒ R = 12180 ÷ 840

⇒ R = 14.5 cm

∴ The correct answer is 14.5 cm.

Additional Information

Circumcentre of a Triangle

It is the point of intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the sides. The distance from the circumcentre to all vertices is equal to the circumradius (R).

Location of Circumcentre

For an acute triangle, it lies inside. For an obtuse triangle, it lies outside. For a right-angled triangle, it lies exactly at the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

Inradius of a Right Triangle

The inradius (r) can be directly found using the formula: r = (a + b − c) ÷ 2, where a and b are perpendicular sides and c is the hypotenuse.

questions.q: On a 2200 m long circular track, Sarita and Kavita drove their cycles from the same point but in opposite direction with the speeds 20 km/hr and 16 km/hr, respectively. After how much time will they meet again for the first time?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since they move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative Speed = 20 + 16 = 36 km/hr

Convert relative speed to m/s: 36 × (5 ÷ 18) = 10 m/s

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 2200 ÷ 10 = 220 seconds

220 seconds = 3 minutes 40 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes 40 seconds.

Alternate Method

Given:

Track length (Distance) = 2200 m

Speed of Sarita = 20 km/hr

Speed of Kavita = 16 km/hr



Formula Used:

Relative Speed (when moving in opposite directions) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculation:

⇒ Relative Speed = 20 + 16 = 36 km/hr

⇒ Speed in m/s = 36 × (5 ÷ 18) = 10 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = 2200 ÷ 10

⇒ Time = 220 seconds

⇒ Convert seconds into minutes: 220 ÷ 60 = 3 minutes and 40 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes 40 seconds.

Additional Information

Meeting in Same Direction

When moving in the same direction on a circular track, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|. Time to meet = Distance ÷ |S₁ − S₂|.

Meeting at Starting Point

To find when multiple runners meet exactly at the starting point again, calculate the LCM of the times taken by each individual to complete one full round.

Conversion Factor

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by (5 ÷ 18). To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).

questions.q: In a triangle HJK, HJ = HK. G is a point on HJ such that HG = GK = JK. What is the degree measure of two-third of (∠HGK + ∠GKJ)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let ∠H = x. In isosceles ΔHGK (HG = GK), ∠GKH = x, making exterior ∠JGK = 2x.

In isosceles ΔGKJ (GK = JK), ∠GJK = 2x. Since HJ = HK, ∠HKJ = ∠HJK = 2x.

Angle sum of ΔHJK: x + 2x + 2x = 180° ⇒ x = 36°.

∠HGK = 180° − 2x = 108° and ∠GKJ = 180° − 4x = 36°.

Required value = ²⁄₃ × (108° + 36°) = ²⁄₃ × 144° = 96°.

∴ The correct answer is 96°.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ HJ = HK

⇒ HG = GK = JK



Calculations:

⇒ Let ∠H = x.

⇒ HG = GK ⇒ ∠GKH = ∠H = x.

⇒ Exterior ∠JGK = ∠H + ∠GKH = 2x.

⇒ GK = JK ⇒ ∠GJK = ∠JGK = 2x ⇒ ∠HJK = 2x.

⇒ HJ = HK ⇒ ∠HKJ = ∠HJK = 2x.

⇒ ΔHJK angle sum: ∠H + ∠HJK + ∠HKJ = 180°

⇒ x + 2x + 2x = 180° ⇒ 5x = 180° ⇒ x = 36°.

⇒ ∠HGK = 180° − 2x = 180° − 72° = 108°.

⇒ ∠GKJ = 180° − 4x = 180° − 144° = 36°.

⇒ ²⁄₃ × (∠HGK + ∠GKJ) = ²⁄₃ × (108° + 36°)

⇒ ²⁄₃ × 144° = 96°.

∴ The correct answer is 96°.

Additional Information

Isosceles Triangle Property

In a triangle, angles opposite to equal sides are always equal in measure.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite non-adjacent interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles in any type of triangle is always exactly 180°.

questions.q: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 at 6.5% per annum rate of interest for the period from 14 February 2023 to 28 April 2023
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total time from 14 Feb to 28 Apr = 14 + 31 + 28 = 73 days.

Convert days to years: 73 ÷ 365 = 1/5 years.

SI = P × R × T ÷ 100

SI = 2000 × 6.5 × (1/5) ÷ 100 = 20 × 1.3

SI = 26

∴ The correct answer is ₹26.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹2000

Rate of interest (R) = 6.5% per annum

Time period = 14 February 2023 to 28 April 2023

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

where T is time in years.



Calculations:

⇒ Count the exact number of days from 14 Feb 2023 to 28 Apr 2023.

⇒ Since 2023 is not a leap year, February has 28 days.

⇒ Days in February (excluding the starting day) = 28 − 14 = 14 days

⇒ Days in March = 31 days

⇒ Days in April = 28 days

⇒ Total days = 14 + 31 + 28 = 73 days

⇒ Time in years (T) = 73 ÷ 365 = 1/5 years

⇒ Substitute values into the Simple Interest formula:

⇒ SI = (2000 × 6.5 × 1) ÷ (100 × 5)

⇒ SI = (20 × 6.5) ÷ 5

⇒ SI = 130 ÷ 5 = 26

∴ The correct answer is ₹26.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI) vs Compound Interest (CI)

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal amount, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal as well as the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Time Calculation Rule

When calculating simple interest between two exact dates, it is standard practice to exclude the first date and include the last date (or vice versa), such that the total number of days strictly equals the mathematical difference between dates.

Converting Days to Years

If the time period is given in days, T is obtained by dividing the total number of days by 365. Frequent standard test values include 73 days (1/5 years) and 146 days (2/5 years).

questions.q: The population of a place increased to 50,000 from 2016 to 2018 at the rate of 6% per annum, and continued the same trend for the next 3 years. If A is the population in 2016 and B is the population in 2020, both are approximated to the next possible integers, then the value of B - A is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Effective % increase for 2 years at 6% p.a. = 6 + 6 + (6 × 6)/100 = 12.36%

Multiplying factor for 2 years = 1.1236

Population in 2020 (B) = 50,000 × 1.1236 = 56,180

Population in 2016 (A) = 50,000 ÷ 1.1236 ≈ 44,500 (approximated to next integer)

Difference B − A = 56,180 − 44,500 = 11,680

∴ The correct answer is 11680.

Alternate Method

Given:

Population in 2018 = 50,000

Rate of increase = 6% per annum

A = Population in 2016, B = Population in 2020

Formula Used:

Population after n years = Initial Population × (1 + R/100)ⁿ



Calculation:

⇒ Time period from 2016 to 2018 = 2 years

⇒ 50,000 = A × (1 + 6/100)²

⇒ A = 50,000 ÷ 1.1236 = 44499.82 ≈ 44,500

⇒ Time period from 2018 to 2020 = 2 years

⇒ B = 50,000 × (1 + 6/100)²

⇒ B = 50,000 × 1.1236 = 56,180

⇒ Value of B − A = 56,180 − 44,500 = 11,680

∴ The correct answer is 11680.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes successively by a% and then b%, the effective percentage change is calculated as: a + b + (a × b) / 100.

Population Growth Formula

If the initial population is P and it grows at a compound rate of R% per annum, the population after n years is given by: P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ.

Depreciation Formula

If the value or population decreases at R% per annum, the value after n years is given by: P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.

questions.q: If the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is 121 : 225, then find the ratio of their corresponding sides.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The ratio of corresponding sides of similar triangles is exactly equal to the square root of the ratio of their areas.

⇒ Ratio of corresponding sides = √121 : √225

⇒ Ratio of corresponding sides = 11 : 15

∴ The correct answer is 11 : 15.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of the areas of two similar triangles = 121 : 225

Formula Used:

For any two similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area₁ / Area₂ = (Side₁ / Side₂)²

Area = 121

Area = 225

Calculations:

Let the areas of the two similar triangles be A₁ and A₂, and their corresponding sides be S₁ and S₂ respectively.

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = 121 / 225

⇒ (S₁ / S₂)² = 121 / 225

Taking the square root on both sides,

⇒ S₁ / S₂ = √(121 / 225)

⇒ S₁ / S₂ = 11 / 15

⇒ S₁ : S₂ = 11 : 15

∴ The correct answer is 11 : 15.

Additional Information

Ratio of Perimeters

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is directly equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of Medians and Altitudes

The ratio of the corresponding medians, corresponding altitudes, and corresponding angle bisectors of two similar triangles is exactly equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Volumes of Similar Solid Figures

If two solid geometric figures are similar, the ratio of their volumes is equal to the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions (V₁ / V₂ = (S₁ / S₂)³).

questions.q: Find the value of Y, if X - 2Y + 2Z = 16, X - Y + Z = 9 and 2X - 3Y - Z = 9.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Multiply the second equation by 2 to get: 2X − 2Y + 2Z = 18.

Subtract the first equation from this result: (2X − 2Y + 2Z) − (X − 2Y + 2Z) = 18 − 16 ⇒ X = 2.

Substitute X = 2 into equations 2 and 3 to get: −Y + Z = 7 and −3Y − Z = 5.

Add these two new equations to eliminate Z: (−Y + Z) + (−3Y − Z) = 7 + 5 ⇒ −4Y = 12 ⇒ Y = −3.

∴ The correct answer is -3.

Alternate Method

Given:

X − 2Y + 2Z = 16 --- (1)

X − Y + Z = 9 --- (2)

2X − 3Y − Z = 9 --- (3)

Calculations:

⇒ From equation (2), express Z in terms of X and Y: Z = 9 − X + Y

⇒ Substitute the value of Z in equation (1):

⇒ X − 2Y + 2(9 − X + Y) = 16

⇒ X − 2Y + 18 − 2X + 2Y = 16

⇒ −X + 18 = 16

⇒ X = 2

⇒ Substitute X = 2 in equation (2):

⇒ 2 − Y + Z = 9

⇒ −Y + Z = 7 --- (4)

⇒ Substitute X = 2 in equation (3):

⇒ 2(2) − 3Y − Z = 9

⇒ 4 − 3Y − Z = 9

⇒ −3Y − Z = 5 --- (5)

⇒ Adding equations (4) and (5):

⇒ (−Y + Z) + (−3Y − Z) = 7 + 5

⇒ −4Y = 12

⇒ Y = −3

∴ The correct answer is -3.

Additional Information

System of Linear Equations

A set of two or more linear equations with the same variables. Finding the solution involves calculating the values for the variables that make all equations true simultaneously.

Elimination Method

This technique solves a system of equations by multiplying equations by constants and then adding or subtracting them to cancel out one of the variables, making the system easier to solve.

Substitution Method

A systematic method where one equation is algebraically solved for one variable, and that result is plugged into the other equations to reduce the number of unknown variables.

Efficiencies: Rani = 48 ÷ 12 = 4 units/day, Adya = 48 ÷ 16 = 3 units/day.

Work done in 2 days (Rani + Adya) = 4 + 3 = 7 units.

Work in 12 days (6 cycles) = 6 × 7 = 42 units. Remaining work = 48 − 42 = 6 units.

Day 13: Rani does 4 units. Remaining = 2 units. Day 14: Adya takes 2/3 day to finish.

∴ The correct answer is 13 ²/₃ days.

Alternate Days Work

When individuals work on alternate days, find the total work done in one complete cycle (usually 2 days) and use it to find the maximum possible full cycles before calculating the leftover work.

Work and Efficiency Ratio

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to Time and Work, an inlet pipe has a positive efficiency (filling) while an outlet pipe has a negative efficiency (emptying).

Shortcut Trick

Direct formula for the exact occurrence of one event out of two independent events:

P(Exactly one) = P(A) + P(B) − 2 × P(A) × P(B)

⇒ P = 2/3 + 3/4 − 2 × (2/3 × 3/4)

⇒ P = 17/12 − 12/12 = 5/12

∴ The correct answer is 5/12.

Alternate Method

Given:

Probability that player A hits the target, P(A) = 2/3

Probability that player B hits the target, P(B) = 3/4

⇒ P(Exactly one hits) = [P(A) × P(B')] + [P(A') × P(B)]

Additional Information

Independent Events

Two events are considered independent if the occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the other. The key formula used is: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).

Mutually Exclusive Events

Events that cannot occur at the same time are mutually exclusive. For such events, the probability of both occurring is zero. The key formula used is: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).

Probability of 'At Least One' Event

The probability that at least one of the independent events occurs is easily calculated by subtracting the probability of none occurring from 1. Formula: P(At least one) = 1 − P(None).

questions.q: On the occasion of Republic Day, a retail store offers a scheme where customers can avail a discount of 26% on their total purchase. If Manish buys items worth ₹2,050, how much money (in ₹) will he save through the scheme discount?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Savings = Discount % × Total Purchase Value

Savings = 26% of 2050

Savings = 26 × 20.5 = 533

∴ The correct answer is ₹533.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total purchase amount = ₹2,050

Discount percentage = 26%

Formula Used:

Discount Amount = (Discount % ÷ 100) × Total Value



Calculations:

⇒ Savings = (26 ÷ 100) × 2050

⇒ Savings = 0.26 × 2050

⇒ Savings = 26 × 20.5

⇒ Savings = 533

∴ The correct answer is ₹533.

Additional Information

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price or the initial Total Value. Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the effective net discount % = a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.

Percentage Base Change

When calculating savings, the original purchase amount always acts as the 100% base value.

questions.q: Vessel A contains milk and water in the ratio 4 : 5. Vessel B contains milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1. If x litres mixture of A is mixed with y litres mixture of B, then the ratio of milk to water in the mixture becomes 8 : 5. Find the ratio x : y.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Fraction of milk in A = 4/9, B = 2/3, and Final Mixture = 8/13.

By Alligation cross-multiplication on the fraction of milk:

Ratio of A to B = (2/3 − 8/13) : (8/13 − 4/9)

⇒ Ratio = 2/39 : 20/117

⇒ Ratio = (2 × 117) : (39 × 20) = 234 : 780

⇒ x : y = 3 : 10

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 10.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of milk to water in vessel A = 4 : 5

Ratio of milk to water in vessel B = 2 : 1

Ratio of milk to water in the final mixture = 8 : 5

Formula Used:

The rule of alligation is applied on the fraction of milk to find the required ratio of mixtures.



Calculations:

⇒ Fraction of milk in Vessel A = 4 / (4 + 5) = 4/9

⇒ Fraction of milk in Vessel B = 2 / (2 + 1) = 2/3

⇒ Fraction of milk in the final mixture = 8 / (8 + 5) = 8/13

⇒ Ratio of x to y = (Fraction in B − Mean Fraction) : (Mean Fraction − Fraction in A)

⇒ x : y = (2/3 − 8/13) : (8/13 − 4/9)

⇒ x : y = [(26 − 24) / 39] : [(72 − 52) / 117]

⇒ x : y = (2 / 39) : (20 / 117)

⇒ x : y = (2 / 39) × (117 / 20)

⇒ x : y = 117 / (39 × 10)

⇒ x : y = 3 : 10

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 10.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

When two ingredients of different prices or concentrations are mixed, the ratio of their quantities is given by: (Quantity of Cheaper) / (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) / (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper).

Concentration in Mixtures

The fraction of any specific component in a mixture is calculated as the quantity of that component divided by the total volume of all components present in the mixture.

Replacement Method

If V is the total volume and x quantity is removed and replaced by water n times, the remaining quantity of pure liquid = V × (1 − x/V)ⁿ.

questions.q: Find the volume (in cm³, rounded off to 2 decimal places) of a right circular cone of diameter 12 cm and height 5 cm. [Use pi=722​]
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

Volume of Cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 6² × 5

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 12 × 5 = 1320 ÷ 7

⇒ Volume = 188.5714... ≈ 188.57 cm³

∴ The correct answer is 188.57 cm³.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of the base (d) = 12 cm

Height of the cone (h) = 5 cm

Value of π = 22/7

Formula Used:

Radius (r) = d ÷ 2

Volume of a right circular cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h



Calculations:

⇒ Radius (r) = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × (6)² × 5

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 36 × 5

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 12 × 5

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 60

⇒ Volume = 1320 ÷ 7

⇒ Volume = 188.5714... cm³

⇒ Rounding off to 2 decimal places, Volume ≈ 188.57 cm³

∴ The correct answer is 188.57 cm³.

Additional Information

Slant Height of a Cone

The slant height (l) is calculated using Pythagoras theorem: l = √(r² + h²).

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved surface of a cone is given by: CSA = π × r × l.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of the curved surface area and the base area: TSA = π × r × (r + l).

Volume of a Cylinder

For a given radius and height, the volume of a cylinder is exactly three times the volume of a cone: V = π × r² × h.

questions.q: If x = 8 + √5 and y = 8 - √5 then the value of x² + y² is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For conjugate surds of the form x = a + √b and y = a − √b, the sum of their squares is given directly by: x² + y² = 2(a² + b)

Here, a = 8 and b = 5.

⇒ x² + y² = 2(8² + 5)

⇒ x² + y² = 2(64 + 5) = 2 × 69 = 138

∴ The correct answer is 138.

Alternate Method

Given:

x = 8 + √5

y = 8 − √5

Formula Used:

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

Calculations:

⇒ x² = (8 + √5)² = 8² + (√5)² + 2 × 8 × √5

⇒ x² = 64 + 5 + 16√5 = 69 + 16√5

⇒ y² = (8 − √5)² = 8² + (√5)² − 2 × 8 × √5

⇒ y² = 64 + 5 − 16√5 = 69 − 16√5

Adding the expanded values of x² and y²:

⇒ x² + y² = (69 + 16√5) + (69 − 16√5)

⇒ x² + y² = 69 + 69 = 138

∴ The correct answer is 138.

Additional Information

Algebraic Expansion Identity

The sum of the squares of the sum and difference of two numbers directly simplifies to: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²).

Difference of Squares

The product of the sum and difference of two numbers yields the difference of their squares: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

Properties of Surds

When multiplying a square root by itself, the root sign is removed: √x × √x = x. The conjugate of an irrational number a + √b is a − √b.

questions.q: A sum of money is to be distributed among 3 friends P, Q and R in the proportion of 5 : 3 : 4. If P gets ₹1,500 more than R, what is Q's share?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference in ratio parts of P and R = 5 − 4 = 1 part.

Given difference = ₹1,500, so 1 part = ₹1,500.

Q's share is 3 parts.

Q's share = 3 × 1,500 = ₹4,500.

∴ The correct answer is ₹4,500.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of shares of P, Q, and R = 5 : 3 : 4

P gets ₹1,500 more than R.



Calculations:

⇒ Let the individual shares of P, Q, and R be 5x, 3x, and 4x respectively.

⇒ According to the condition, P's share − R's share = 1500

⇒ 5x − 4x = 1500

⇒ x = 1500

⇒ Q's share = 3x

⇒ Q's share = 3 × 1500 = 4500

∴ The correct answer is ₹4,500.

Additional Information

Properties of Ratio

Multiplying or dividing all terms of a ratio by the same non-zero number does not change the ratio. It is universally used to scale down or parameterise given quantities.

Sum of Shares in Proportion

If the total sum is given and needs to be divided in the ratio A : B : C, an individual share (e.g., A's share) is calculated directly as: (A ÷ (A + B + C)) × Total Sum.

Difference Between Shares

When the difference between two parts is known, the numeric value of 1 ratio part is equal to the given difference amount divided by the difference in their ratio parts. This skips algebraic variables.

questions.q: If tan (x + y) tan (x - y) = 1, then find the value of tanx.
options: 3​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If tan A × tan B = 1, then A + B = 90°.

Given: tan (x + y) × tan (x − y) = 1

⇒ (x + y) + (x − y) = 90°

⇒ 2x = 90° ⇒ x = 45°

⇒ tan x = tan 45° = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given:

tan (x + y) tan (x − y) = 1

Formula Used:

tan (A + B) = (tan A + tan B) ÷ (1 − tan A tan B)

tan (A − B) = (tan A − tan B) ÷ (1 + tan A tan B)

Calculations:

⇒ [(tan x + tan y) ÷ (1 − tan x tan y)] × [(tan x − tan y) ÷ (1 + tan x tan y)] = 1

⇒ (tan²x − tan²y) ÷ (1 − tan²x tan²y) = 1

⇒ tan²x − tan²y = 1 − tan²x tan²y

⇒ tan²x + tan²x tan²y = 1 + tan²y

⇒ tan²x (1 + tan²y) = 1 + tan²y

⇒ tan²x = 1

⇒ tan x = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Complementary Angle Properties

If A + B = 90°, then sin A = cos B, tan A = cot B, and sec A = cosec B.

Important Trigonometric Rules

If tan A × tan B = 1, then A + B = 90°. Similarly, if sin A × sec B = 1, then A + B = 90°.

Double Angle Formulas

tan 2A = (2 tan A) ÷ (1 − tan²A)

questions.q: If sectheta+tanthetasectheta−tantheta​ = 91​, θ lies in the first quadrant, then the value of sintheta+tan2thetasintheta−tan2theta​ is:
options: -2713​
2713​
2911​
-2911​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using Componendo and Dividendo on (secθ + tanθ) / (secθ − tanθ) = 9 / 1:

⇒ secθ / tanθ = (9 + 1) / (9 − 1) ⇒ 1 / sinθ = 10 / 8 = 5 / 4 ⇒ sinθ = 4/5

Since sinθ = 4/5, in a right-angled triangle, Opposite = 4, Hypotenuse = 5, Adjacent = 3. Thus, tanθ = 4/3.

⇒ Value = (sinθ − tan²θ) / (sinθ + tan²θ) = (4/5 − 16/9) / (4/5 + 16/9)

⇒ (−44 / 45) ÷ (116 / 45) = −44 / 116 = −11/29

∴ The correct answer is −11/29.

Alternate Method

Given:

(secθ − tanθ) / (secθ + tanθ) = 1/9

Formula Used:

secθ = 1 / cosθ, tanθ = sinθ / cosθ

Calculations:

⇒ [(1/cosθ) − (sinθ/cosθ)] / [(1/cosθ) + (sinθ/cosθ)] = 1/9

⇒ (1 − sinθ) / (1 + sinθ) = 1/9

⇒ 9 × (1 − sinθ) = 1 + sinθ

⇒ 9 − 9sinθ = 1 + sinθ

⇒ 10sinθ = 8

⇒ sinθ = 8/10 = 4/5

Since θ lies in the first quadrant, we can visualize this using a right-angled triangle:



⇒ Opposite = 4, Hypotenuse = 5

⇒ Adjacent = √(Hypotenuse² − Opposite²) = √(5² − 4²) = √(25 − 16) = √9 = 3

⇒ tanθ = Opposite / Adjacent = 4/3

⇒ tan²θ = (4/3)² = 16/9

Now, substituting the values into the required expression:

⇒ (sinθ − tan²θ) / (sinθ + tan²θ)

⇒ (4/5 − 16/9) / (4/5 + 16/9)

⇒ [(36 − 80) / 45] / [(36 + 80) / 45]

⇒ (−44 / 45) / (116 / 45)

⇒ −44 / 116

⇒ −11/29

∴ The correct answer is −11/29.

Additional Information

Componendo and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then a−ba+b​ = c−dc+d​. This algebraic property is highly effective for rapidly simplifying equations that consist of sum and difference pairs in the numerator and denominator.

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of integers satisfying a² + b² = c² is called a triplet. Remembering fundamental sets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) significantly improves speed in geometry and trigonometry problems.

Trigonometric Quadrant Rules (ASTC Rule)

In the 1st Quadrant, All trigonometric functions are positive. In the 2nd Quadrant, only Sine is positive. In the 3rd Quadrant, only Tangent is positive. In the 4th Quadrant, only Cosine is positive. Since θ lies in the first quadrant here, tanθ and sinθ are both positive.

questions.q: By how much is 60% of 75 greater than 51​ of 25?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

60% is equal to the fraction 3/5.

First value = 3/5 × 75 = 45

Second value = 1/5 × 25 = 5

Difference = 45 − 5 = 40

∴ The correct answer is 40.

Alternate Method

Given:

First expression = 60% of 75

Second expression = 1/5 of 25

Method Used:

Convert the percentage to a fraction and apply the BODMAS rule, where 'Of' is treated as multiplication.

Calculations:

⇒ First expression = (60 ÷ 100) × 75

⇒ First expression = (3 ÷ 5) × 75 = 3 × 15 = 45

⇒ Second expression = (1 ÷ 5) × 25

⇒ Second expression = 5

⇒ Difference = 45 − 5 = 40

∴ The correct answer is 40.

Additional Information

BODMAS Rule

In mathematical expressions, 'Of' signifies multiplication and is resolved before standard division and multiplication, according to the BODMAS sequence (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting percentages to standard fractions speeds up calculations. Common fraction equivalents include 20% = 1/5, 40% = 2/5, 60% = 3/5, and 80% = 4/5.

Base Value in Percentages

The term 'Percentage' means 'per hundred'. Thus, an expression like x% of y is mathematically calculated as (x ÷ 100) × y.

questions.q: If the average age of three persons is 56 years and their ages are in the ratio 2 : 5 : 7, then find the age of the youngest person.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Average of ratio parts = (2 + 5 + 7) ÷ 3 = 14/3 parts

14/3 parts → 56 years

1 part → (56 × 3) ÷ 14 = 12 years

Youngest person's age = 2 parts = 2 × 12 = 24 years

∴ The correct answer is 24 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average age of 3 persons = 56 years

Ratio of their ages = 2 : 5 : 7

Formula Used:

Total Sum = Average × Number of observations



Calculations:

⇒ Total age of the three persons = 56 × 3 = 168 years

⇒ Let the ages of the persons be 2x, 5x, and 7x respectively.

⇒ Sum of ages = 2x + 5x + 7x = 14x

⇒ 14x = 168

⇒ x = 168 ÷ 14

⇒ x = 12

⇒ Age of the youngest person = 2x = 2 × 12 = 24 years

∴ The correct answer is 24 years.

Additional Information

Sum and Average Relation

The sum of all values in a dataset is always equal to the average multiplied by the total number of values. Sum = Average × N.

Proportional Distribution

When a total quantity is divided among multiple parts in a given ratio (a : b : c), the share of the first part is calculated as (a ÷ (a + b + c)) × Total Quantity.

questions.q: A toy is in the form of a cone mounted on a hemisphere. The radius of the hemisphere and that of the cone is 36 cm and height of the cone is 105 cm . The total surface area (in cm²) of the toy is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Surface Area (TSA) of the toy = CSA of cone + CSA of hemisphere = πr(l + 2r)

Slant height, l = √(r² + h²) = √(36² + 105²) = √(1296 + 11025) = √12321 = 111 cm

TSA = π × 36 × (111 + 2 × 36)

TSA = π × 36 × (111 + 72)

TSA = π × 36 × 183 = 6588π cm²

∴ The correct answer is 6588π cm².

Alternate Method



Given:

Radius of hemisphere and cone, r = 36 cm

Height of the cone, h = 105 cm

Formula Used:

Slant height of cone, l = √(r² + h²)

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of cone = πrl

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of hemisphere = 2πr²

Calculation:

⇒ First, let's find the slant height (l) of the conical portion.

⇒ l = √(36² + 105²)

⇒ l = √(1296 + 11025)

⇒ l = √12321 = 111 cm

⇒ CSA of the cone = π × 36 × 111 = 3996π cm²

⇒ CSA of the hemisphere = 2 × π × (36)²

⇒ CSA of the hemisphere = 2 × π × 1296 = 2592π cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = CSA of cone + CSA of hemisphere

⇒ Total Surface Area = 3996π + 2592π

⇒ Total Surface Area = 6588π cm²

∴ The correct answer is 6588π cm².

Additional Information

Volume of Cone

The volume of a cone is calculated as one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height: V = (1 ÷ 3)πr²h.

Volume of Hemisphere

Since a hemisphere is exactly half of a full sphere, its volume is given by the formula V = (2 ÷ 3)πr³.

Total Surface Area of Solid Hemisphere

If the hemisphere stands alone as a solid body, its total surface area includes the curved surface and the flat circular base: TSA = 3πr².

questions.q: Anil and Beena are friends, and the difference between their ages is 5 years. Anil's father Dinesh is three times as old as Anil, and Beena is twice as old as her sister Charu. The ages of Dinesh and Charu differ by 45 years. If Beena is older than Anil, then find the sum of the present ages of both Dinesh and Charu.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Anil's age be A.

Dinesh = 3A and Charu = (A + 5) ÷ 2.

Given difference: 3A − (A + 5) ÷ 2 = 45

⇒ 6A − A − 5 = 90 ⇒ A = 19

Dinesh = 57 years, Charu = 12 years ⇒ Sum = 69 years.

∴ The correct answer is 69 years.

Alternate Method



Given:

Difference between Beena and Anil's age = 5 years (Beena is older)

Dinesh's age = 3 × Anil's age

Beena's age = 2 × Charu's age

Difference between Dinesh and Charu's age = 45 years

Calculations:

Let Anil's age be A.

⇒ Beena's age (B) = A + 5

⇒ Dinesh's age (D) = 3 × A = 3A

⇒ Charu's age (C) = B ÷ 2 = (A + 5) ÷ 2

Since Dinesh is Anil's father, his age is evidently greater than Charu's age.

⇒ D − C = 45

⇒ 3A − (A + 5) ÷ 2 = 45

Multiply the entire equation by 2 to remove the fraction:

⇒ 6A − (A + 5) = 90

⇒ 5A − 5 = 90

⇒ 5A = 95

⇒ A = 19 years

Now, substitute the value of A back to find Dinesh and Charu's ages:

⇒ Dinesh's age (D) = 3 × 19 = 57 years

⇒ Charu's age (C) = (19 + 5) ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 years

⇒ Sum of their ages = 57 + 12 = 69 years

∴ The correct answer is 69 years.

Additional Information

Constant Age Difference

The age difference between two individuals is always constant throughout their lives. If person A is 5 years older than person B today, A will always remain 5 years older than B in the future.

Linear Equations in Ages

When a question states relationships like "X is three times as old as Y", it translates directly into a linear equation (X = 3Y). Solving simultaneous linear equations is the primary method to find exact current ages.

Handling Fractional Ages

Statements like "A is twice as old as B" can be written as A = 2B or B = A ÷ 2. It is often mathematically easier to multiply the entire equation by the denominator to avoid working with fractions, as done in the solution step: 6A − (A + 5) = 90.

questions.q: The height of a right circular cone is 63 cm and the area of its curved surface is five times the area of its base. What is the volume (in cm³) of the cone? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given CSA = 5 × Base Area ⇒ πrl = 5πr² ⇒ l = 5r.

Using l² = r² + h² ⇒ 25r² = r² + h² ⇒ 24r² = h².

Since h = 63, r² = 63² ÷ 24 = 3969 ÷ 24 = 1323/8.

Volume = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3) × (22/7) × (1323/8) × 63

Volume = 22 × 441 × 9 ÷ 8 = 43659 ÷ 4 = 10914.75 cm³.

∴ The correct answer is 10914.75 cm³.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height of the cone (h) = 63 cm

Curved Surface Area = 5 × Base Area

Formula Used:

Curved Surface Area of a cone = πrl

Base Area of a cone = πr²

Volume of a cone = (1/3)πr²h

l² = r² + h² (where l is slant height)



Calculations:

⇒ πrl = 5 × πr²

⇒ l = 5r

⇒ l² = 25r²

We know that, l² = r² + h²

⇒ 25r² = r² + 63²

⇒ 24r² = 3969

⇒ r² = 3969 ÷ 24 = 1323 ÷ 8 cm²

Now, Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × r² × h

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × (1323/8) × 63

⇒ Volume = 22 × 441 × 9 ÷ 8

⇒ Volume = 11 × 3969 ÷ 4

⇒ Volume = 43659 ÷ 4 = 10914.75 cm³

∴ The correct answer is 10914.75 cm³.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of a Cone

The total surface area includes the curved surface area and the flat base area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Frustum of a Cone

When a right circular cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base, the lower part is called a frustum. Volume = (1/3)πh(R² + r² + Rr).

Slant Height Relationship

The slant height (l), radius (r), and vertical height (h) always form a right-angled triangle where l² = r² + h².

questions.q: A man buys 10 identical articles for a total of ₹15. If he sells each of them for ₹1.7, then his profit percentage will be _%(rounded off to two decimal place).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Cost Price (CP) of 1 article = 15 ÷ 10 = &rupee;1.5

Selling Price (SP) of 1 article = &rupee;1.7

Profit = 1.7 − 1.5 = &rupee;0.2

Profit % = (0.2 ÷ 1.5) × 100 = 13.33%

∴ The correct answer is 13.33%.

Alternate Method



Given:

Total Cost Price (CP) of 10 articles = &rupee;15

Selling Price (SP) of 1 article = &rupee;1.7

Formula Used:

Total SP = SP of 1 article × Total articles

Profit = Total SP − Total CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Total SP of 10 articles = 1.7 × 10 = &rupee;17

⇒ Total CP of 10 articles = &rupee;15

⇒ Profit = 17 − 15 = &rupee;2

⇒ Profit % = (2 ÷ 15) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 200 ÷ 15 = 13.33%

∴ The correct answer is 13.33%.

Additional Information

Loss Percentage

When Cost Price is greater than Selling Price, a loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Percentage Change

If there are successive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by: a + b + (a × b ÷ 100).

questions.q:
Find the median of the following data. (Rounded off to 2 decimal places.)

Class interval 0-5 5-10 10-15 15-20 20-25 25-30 30-35

Frequency 3 5 4 2 7 6 5
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total frequency N = 32 → N/2 = 16.

Cumulative frequency just > 16 is 21, so median class is 20-25.

L = 20, CF = 14, f = 7, h = 5.

Median = 20 + [(16 − 14) ÷ 7] × 5 = 20 + 10/7 ≈ 21.43.

∴ The correct answer is 21.43.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total frequency (N) = 3 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 7 + 6 + 5 = 32

Cumulative frequencies (CF) for classes: 3, 8, 12, 14, 21, 27, 32

Formula Used:

Median = L + [(N/2 − CF) ÷ f] × h

Calculations:

⇒ N/2 = 32 ÷ 2 = 16

⇒ The CF just greater than 16 is 21, which corresponds to the class interval 20-25.

⇒ Lower limit of median class (L) = 20

⇒ CF of preceding class (CF) = 14

⇒ Frequency of median class (f) = 7

⇒ Class size (h) = 5

⇒ Median = 20 + [(16 − 14) ÷ 7] × 5

⇒ Median = 20 + (2 ÷ 7) × 5

⇒ Median = 20 + 10 ÷ 7

⇒ Median = 20 + 1.428...

⇒ Median ≈ 21.43

∴ The correct answer is 21.43.

Additional Information

Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = L + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h, where f₁ is frequency of modal class, f₀ and f₂ are frequencies of preceding and succeeding classes.

Mean of Grouped Data

Direct method formula: Mean = Σfᵢxᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ represents the class mark (midpoint) of each class interval.

Empirical Relationship

The empirical relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

questions.q: Let ABC be a right-angled triangle with a right angle at B. If tan A = √3, then find the value of sin A cos C + cos A sin C and cos A cos C - sin A sin C.
options: 2√3​, 2√3​

2√3​, 21​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In right-angled ΔABC with ∠B = 90°, the acute angles A and C must sum to 90° (∠A + ∠C = 90°).

We can directly apply compound angle formulas without needing the exact angle values:

⇒ sin A cos C + cos A sin C = sin(A + C) = sin 90° = 1

⇒ cos A cos C − sin A sin C = cos(A + C) = cos 90° = 0

∴ The correct answer is 1, 0.

Alternate Method



Given: In right-angled ΔABC, ∠B = 90° and tan A = √3.

⇒ Since tan 60° = √3, we have ∠A = 60°.

⇒ The sum of angles in a triangle is 180°, so ∠C = 180° − (90° + 60°) = 30°.

Calculating the first expression (sin A cos C + cos A sin C):

⇒ sin 60° cos 30° + cos 60° sin 30°

⇒ (√3/2) × (√3/2) + (1/2) × (1/2)

⇒ 3/4 + 1/4 = 4/4 = 1

Calculating the second expression (cos A cos C − sin A sin C):

⇒ cos 60° cos 30° − sin 60° sin 30°

⇒ (1/2) × (√3/2) − (√3/2) × (1/2)

⇒ √3/4 − √3/4 = 0

∴ The correct answer is 1, 0.

Additional Information

Compound Angle Formulas

sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B
cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B

Complementary Angles

In a right-angled triangle, the two acute angles are complementary, meaning their sum is always equal to 90°.

Standard Trigonometric Values

sin 30° = cos 60° = 1/2
sin 60° = cos 30° = √3/2

questions.q: Simplify (5z - 12y)² + (12z + 5y)² - 144z²
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the direct algebraic identity: (ax − by)² + (bx + ay)² = (a² + b²)(x² + y²)

Here, a = 5, b = 12, x = z, and y = y.

⇒ (5z − 12y)² + (12z + 5y)² = (5² + 12²)(z² + y²)

⇒ (25 + 144)(z² + y²) = 169z² + 169y²

Now, simply subtract 144z²: 169z² + 169y² − 144z² = 25z² + 169y²

∴ The correct answer is 25z² + 169y².

Alternate Method

Given:

(5z − 12y)² + (12z + 5y)² − 144z²

Formula Used:

(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

Calculations:

⇒ (5z − 12y)² = (5z)² − 2 × 5z × 12y + (12y)² = 25z² − 120yz + 144y²

⇒ (12z + 5y)² = (12z)² + 2 × 12z × 5y + (5y)² = 144z² + 120yz + 25y²

Adding both squared expressions together:

⇒ (25z² − 120yz + 144y²) + (144z² + 120yz + 25y²)

⇒ 25z² + 144z² + 144y² + 25y² − 120yz + 120yz

⇒ 169z² + 169y²

Now, substitute this result back into the complete original expression by subtracting 144z²:

⇒ 169z² + 169y² − 144z²

⇒ 25z² + 169y²

∴ The correct answer is 25z² + 169y².

Additional Information

Sum and Difference of Squares

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). This is useful for quickly simplifying expressions with identical terms.

Brahmagupta-Fibonacci Identity

(a² + b²)(x² + y²) = (ax − by)² + (bx + ay)². This identity shows that the product of two sums of two squares is itself a sum of two squares.

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b). This is extensively used in algebraic factorisation and rapid calculation.

questions.q:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

C. These large MNCs with worldwide network look for the cheapest goods in order to maximise their profits.

D. To get these large orders, Indian garment exporters try hard to cut their own costs.

E. Where earlier a factory used to employ workers on a permanent basis, now they employ workers only on a temporary basis so that they do not have to pay workers for the whole year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.

Key Points

• Sentence B should be the first as it introduces the context of Indian garment exporters catering to large MNCs in Europe and America.

• Sentence C should follow as it explains the nature of these large MNCs looking for cheap goods to maximize their profits:

• "These large MNCs with worldwide network look for the cheapest goods in order to maximize their profits."

• Sentence D comes next as it describes how Indian garment exporters attempt to fulfill large orders from MNCs:

• "To get these large orders, Indian garment exporters try hard to cut their own costs."

• Sentence A follows explaining the means which exporters use to reduce costs:

• "As cost of raw materials cannot be reduced, exporters try to cut labour costs."

• Sentence E concludes the paragraph describing the change in employment practices to cut costs:

• "Where earlier a factory used to employ workers on a permanent basis, now they employ workers only on a temporary basis so that they do not have to pay workers for the whole year."

• The correct order is BCDAE.

Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:

"Large MNCs in the garment industry in Europe and America order their products from Indian exporters. As cost of raw materials cannot be reduced, exporters try to cut labour costs. Where earlier a factory used to employ workers on a permanent basis, now they employ workers only on a temporary basis so that they do not have to pay workers for the whole year."

Which of the following sentences is/are true?

i. All isoclines are expansion paths but all expansion paths are not isoclines.

ii. Short-run production functions involve adjusting all inputs, including fixed inputs like land or capital, to affect output.

iii. Stock resources are the resources which are not used in one period of production but can be stored for a later period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only iii.

Key Points

• Stock resources refer to those resources that are available for use but are not consumed during a single period of production.

• These resources can be stored and utilized in future periods, ensuring availability over time.

• Examples of stock resources include raw materials like minerals, fossil fuels, and long-lasting tools and machinery.

• Stock resources are crucial for managing long-term production and ensuring sustainability in various industries.

• Proper management and storage of stock resources can help mitigate resource scarcity and maintain steady production levels.

Additional Information

• Isoclines and Expansion Paths

• An isocline is a curve that represents combinations of inputs that yield the same level of output.

• Expansion paths show the combination of inputs that minimize costs for different levels of output.

• While all isoclines are considered expansion paths, not all expansion paths are isoclines.

• Short-run Production Functions

• In the short run, some inputs, such as capital and land, are fixed and cannot be adjusted.

• Production can be altered by changing variable inputs like labor and raw materials.

• Adjusting fixed inputs is characteristic of long-run production functions, not short-run.

• Flow Resources

• Flow resources are those that are used up in the process of production and cannot be stored for future use.

• Examples include electricity, water, and labor.

• These resources must be continuously available to maintain production.

• Sustainability in Resource Management

• Sustainable resource management involves using resources in a way that meets current needs without compromising future availability.

• Both stock and flow resources must be managed carefully to ensure long-term ecological and economic stability.

• Strategies include recycling, efficient usage, and investing in renewable resources.

questions.q: Which of the following is a monoatomic gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Xenon.

Key Points

• Xenon is a noble gas, which is typically found as a monoatomic gas in nature.

• Xenon is chemically inert and does not readily form compounds with other elements.

• It is one of the rare gases found in the Earth's atmosphere, with a concentration of about 0.0000087% by volume.

• Being monoatomic means that Xenon exists as single atoms rather than molecules.

Additional Information

• Noble Gases

• Noble gases include Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), and Radon (Rn).

• These gases are characterized by their lack of chemical reactivity due to having complete valence electron shells.

• Monoatomic Gases

• Monoatomic gases consist of single atoms not bonded to each other.

• Examples include noble gases like Helium, Neon, and Argon, in addition to Xenon.

• Uses of Xenon

• Xenon is used in flash lamps, arc lamps, and as a general anesthetic.

• It is also utilized in ion propulsion systems for spacecraft.

• Chemical Inertness

• The inertness of noble gases makes them ideal for use in conditions where reactions are undesirable.

• This property is due to their filled outer electron shells, which make them stable and unreactive.

Select the most appropriate answer from the options given below regarding Census 2011.

Statement 2. The percentage decadal growth during 2001-2011 has registered the sharpest decline since Independence.
options: Both statements 1 and 2 are not correct.

The correct answer is Both statements 1 and 2 are correct.

Key Points

• According to the Census 2011, the population of India increased by more than 181 million during the decade 2001-2011.

• The total population of India as per Census 2011 is 1.21 billion.

• The percentage decadal growth rate of India's population during 2001-2011 was 17.64%, which is the sharpest decline since Independence.

• The decadal growth rate during the 1991-2001 period was 21.54%, showing a significant reduction in the growth rate in the subsequent decade.

Additional Information

• Census 2011

• The Census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

• It is a decennial exercise, meaning it is conducted every 10 years.

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872.

• It collects various demographic, socio-economic, and cultural data which is crucial for planning and policy-making.

• Population Growth Rate

• The population growth rate is the rate at which the number of individuals in a population increases in a given time period as a fraction of the initial population.

• It can be expressed as a percentage.

• Decadal Growth Rate

• It refers to the growth rate of a population over a period of ten years.

• It is calculated by the formula: (Population at the end of the decade - Population at the beginning of the decade) / Population at the beginning of the decade * 100

• Demographic Transition

• It is a model that describes population change over time.

• It is based on an interpretation of population trends in terms of birth rate and death rate.

• Countries move from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates through time.

questions.q: What is the name of the ion with a charge of -1?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Anion.

Key Points

• An ion with a charge of -1 is called an anion.

• Anions are formed when an atom gains one or more electrons, resulting in a net negative charge.

• Common examples of anions include chloride (Cl⁻), bromide (Br⁻), and iodide (I⁻).

• Anions play crucial roles in various chemical reactions and are essential in maintaining the charge balance in compounds.

Additional Information

• Cation

• A cation is an ion with a positive charge.

• Cations are formed when an atom loses one or more electrons.

• Examples include sodium (Na⁺), calcium (Ca²⁺), and potassium (K⁺).

• Monovalent Ion

• A monovalent ion has a charge of +1 or -1.

• Examples include hydrogen ion (H⁺) and fluoride ion (F⁻).

• Polyvalent Ion

• A polyvalent ion has a charge greater than +1 or -1.

• Examples include sulfate (SO₄²⁻) and phosphate (PO₄³⁻).

• Ions in Chemical Reactions

• Ions are essential in the formation of ionic compounds.

• Ionic bonds are formed through the electrostatic attraction between cations and anions.

• Understanding ions is crucial for studying electrochemistry and various biological processes.

questions.q: In December 1991, which act was amended to bring public enterprises under the purview of the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) as part of the country's economic reforms program?

Key Points

• In December 1991, the Sick Industrial Companies Act (SICA) was amended to include public enterprises under the purview of the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR).

• The amendment was part of the broader economic reforms initiated by the Indian government to revitalize the industrial sector.

• The primary objective of SICA was to detect sick and potentially sick companies at an early stage and to expedite their revival.

• BIFR was established under SICA to address the problems of industrial sickness and to determine measures for their rehabilitation.

Additional Information

• Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR)

• BIFR was set up in January 1987 under the Sick Industrial Companies Act (SICA).

• Its purpose was to determine the preventive, ameliorative, remedial, and other measures which need to be taken concerning sick industrial companies.

• The board was also empowered to consider measures for the revival and rehabilitation of potentially viable sick industrial companies.

• It could also recommend the winding up of non-viable companies.

• Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985 (SICA)

• SICA was enacted to detect and deal with sick and potentially sick companies in India.

• It aimed to provide timely detection and corrective actions to revive the sick industries.

• The act provided for the constitution of the BIFR to perform such functions.

• SICA was eventually repealed in 2003 with the introduction of the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Repeal Act, 2003.

• Industrial Policy Reforms of 1991

• The 1991 reforms marked a significant shift in the economic policy of India, moving towards liberalization, privatization, and globalization.

• These reforms included deregulation of industries, reduction of import tariffs, and reforms in the financial sector.

• The objective was to promote competitive efficiency and to integrate the Indian economy with the global market.

• The reforms aimed to reduce the role of the public sector and encourage private sector participation in the economy.

• Economic Reforms in India

• The economic reforms of 1991 were initiated in response to a severe balance of payments crisis.

• The reforms included measures to stabilize the economy and to create a more open and market-oriented economy.

• Key reforms included fiscal consolidation, liberalization of trade and investment policies, and financial sector reforms.

• The reforms have significantly contributed to the growth and development of the Indian economy over the past three decades.

questions.q: Which theory, independently introduced in 1923, led to the concept of acid base conjugate pairs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Brønsted-Lowry theory.

Key Points

• The Brønsted-Lowry theory was independently introduced in 1923 by Johannes Nicolaus Brønsted and Thomas Martin Lowry.

• This theory defines acids as proton donors and bases as proton acceptors.

• It led to the concept of conjugate acid-base pairs, where an acid and a base differ by the presence or absence of a proton.

• Brønsted-Lowry theory expanded the definition of acids and bases beyond aqueous solutions.

Additional Information

• Arrhenius Theory:

• Proposed by Svante Arrhenius in 1887.

• Defines acids as substances that increase the concentration of H₃O⁺ ions in aqueous solution.

• Bases are substances that increase the concentration of OH− ions in aqueous solution.

• Lewis Theory:

• Proposed by Gilbert N. Lewis in 1923.

• Defines acids as electron pair acceptors and bases as electron pair donors.

• Expands the concept of acids and bases to include reactions without protons.

• Davy's Theory:

• Proposed by Humphry Davy in the early 19th century.

• Suggested that acids contain replaceable hydrogen atoms.

• Davy's work helped to lay the groundwork for modern acid-base theories.

• Conjugate Acid-Base Pairs:

• In the Brønsted-Lowry theory, acids and bases form conjugate pairs.

• When an acid donates a proton, it forms its conjugate base.

• When a base accepts a proton, it forms its conjugate acid.

questions.q: Identify the naturally occurring aluminum oxide mineral that usually forms hexagonal barrel-shaped prisms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Corundum.

Key Points

• Corundum is a naturally occurring aluminum oxide mineral (Al2O3).

• It commonly forms hexagonal barrel-shaped prisms, which can be terminated by flat surfaces.

• Corundum is renowned for its hardness, scoring a 9 on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness.

• This mineral is the primary source of gem-quality sapphires and rubies.

• Corundum is typically found in metamorphic rocks such as schist and marble.

Additional Information

• Mohs Scale of Mineral Hardness:

• It is a qualitative ordinal scale characterizing scratch resistance of various minerals.

• Devised by the German geologist and mineralogist Friedrich Mohs in 1812.

• It ranges from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond).

• Sapphires and Rubies:

• Both are varieties of corundum distinguished by color.

• Rubies are red due to the presence of chromium.

• Sapphires can be blue, yellow, or even colorless.

• Metamorphic Rocks:

• Formed through the transformation of pre-existing rocks under high pressure and temperature.

• Examples include schist, marble, and gneiss.

• Industrial Uses of Corundum:

• Used as an abrasive due to its hardness.

• Employed in cutting tools and grinding wheels.

• Also utilized in the manufacture of refractory materials.

questions.q: Mathura was the second capital of _ dynasty.

Key Points

• The Kushana dynasty was a prominent dynasty in ancient India, known for its significant role in the development of culture and trade.

• Kanishka the Great:

• Kanishka was a renowned emperor of the Kushana dynasty, ruling during the 2nd century CE.

• He is credited with organizing the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir, which led to the formal adoption of Mahayana Buddhism.

• Kanishka is also known for his patronage of art, architecture, and the establishment of the Silk Road.

• Kushana Coinage:

• The Kushanas introduced gold coinage in India, which featured the images of their kings and various deities.

• Their coins played a significant role in facilitating trade and commerce in the region.

• Gandhara Art:

• The Kushana period saw the flourishing of Gandhara art, which is a unique blend of Indian and Greco-Roman artistic traditions.

• This style is particularly noted for its exquisite Buddhist sculptures and stupas.

• Silk Road:

• The Kushanas played a pivotal role in the development of the Silk Road, which was a network of trade routes connecting the East and West.

• This facilitated cultural exchanges and the spread of Buddhism across Asia.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

Statements:

1) Ampere's Law describes the relationship between electric current and the magnetic field it produces.

2) Maxwell's equations are a set of four fundamental equations governing electric and magnetic fields in the absence of charges and currents.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.

Key Points

• Ampere's Law describes the relationship between electric current and the magnetic field it produces.

• According to Ampere's Law, the magnetic field in space around an electric current is proportional to the electric current which serves as its source.

• Ampere’s Law is mathematically expressed as ∮B·dl = μ₀I, where B is the magnetic field, dl is a differential element of the path, μ₀ is the permeability of free space, and I is the current enclosed by the path.

• Maxwell's equations govern electric and magnetic fields, but they also account for the presence of charges and currents, not just their absence.

Additional Information

• Maxwell's Equations

• Maxwell's equations consist of four fundamental laws: Gauss's law, Gauss's law for magnetism, Faraday's law of induction, and Ampere's law (with Maxwell's addition).

• These equations describe how electric and magnetic fields are generated by charges, currents, and changes of the fields.

• In the presence of charges and currents, Maxwell's equations provide a complete set of rules for the behavior of electric and magnetic fields.

• Gauss's Law

• Gauss's Law states that the electric flux through a closed surface is proportional to the charge enclosed by the surface.

• Mathematically, it is expressed as ∮E·dA = Q/ε₀, where E is the electric field, dA is a differential area on the closed surface, Q is the total charge enclosed, and ε₀ is the permittivity of free space.

• Faraday's Law of Induction

• Faraday's Law of Induction states that a change in magnetic field within a closed loop induces an electromotive force (EMF) in the wire loop.

• This is mathematically represented as ε = -dΦB/dt, where ε is the induced EMF and ΦB is the magnetic flux.

• Permeability and Permittivity

• The permeability of free space (μ₀) is a constant that characterizes the ability of a material to support the formation of a magnetic field within itself.

• The permittivity of free space (ε₀) is a constant that characterizes the ability of a material to transmit an electric field within itself.

questions.q: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease is caused by duplication of the peripheral myelin protein-22 (PMP22) gene on which chromosome?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is chromosome 17.

Key Points

• Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) is one of the most common inherited neurological disorders, affecting the peripheral nerves.

• It is specifically caused by the duplication of the PMP22 gene located on chromosome 17.

• The disease leads to the progressive loss of muscle tissue and touch sensation, primarily in the feet, legs, hands, and arms.

• CMT can be classified into several types, with CMT1A being the most common form linked to the duplication of PMP22.

• Diagnosis often involves genetic testing to identify the duplication of the PMP22 gene on chromosome 17.

Additional Information

• PMP22 Gene:

• The Peripheral Myelin Protein 22 (PMP22) gene plays a crucial role in the structure and function of myelin, the protective sheath around nerves.

• Overexpression of PMP22 due to gene duplication disrupts the production of normal myelin, leading to nerve degeneration.

• Symptoms of CMT:

• Common symptoms include muscle weakness, decreased muscle size, decreased sensation in extremities, foot deformities, and difficulty walking.

• Symptoms typically appear in adolescence or early adulthood.

• Types of CMT:

• CMT1: Caused by abnormalities in myelin.

• CMT2: Caused by abnormalities in the axon of the peripheral nerve cell.

• CMTX: X-linked inheritance pattern, often affecting males more severely.

• Treatment and Management:

• There is currently no cure for CMT; treatment focuses on managing symptoms.

Key Points

• Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel served as the first Home Minister of Independent India.

• He played a crucial role in the integration of princely states into the Indian Union.

• Integration of Princely States:

• Sardar Patel successfully integrated over 560 princely states into the Indian Union post-independence.

• He used diplomacy and, where necessary, force to ensure the states joined India.

• Iron Man of India:

• Sardar Patel is often referred to as the "Iron Man of India" for his strong leadership and decisive actions.

• Bharat Ratna:

questions.q: What was the status of the agricultural sector in India before the Green Revolution?
options: Use of old technology and the absence of required infrastructure
Use of advanced technology and high productivity
Use of advanced technology and dependency on rainfall
Use of traditional technology and the abundance of required infrastructure
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Use of old technology and the absence of required infrastructure.

Key Points

• Before the Green Revolution, Indian agriculture relied heavily on traditional farming techniques that were not very efficient.

• The yield per hectare was significantly low compared to other countries due to the use of outdated methods.

• There was a lack of proper irrigation facilities, making agriculture highly dependent on monsoon rains.

• The agricultural sector faced frequent crop failures and low productivity, leading to food shortages and economic instability.

• Modern infrastructure such as cold storage and transportation facilities were largely absent, leading to significant post-harvest losses.

Additional Information

• Green Revolution

• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that took place between the 1940s and the late 1960s.

• It involved the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, increased use of fertilizers and pesticides, and the development of better irrigation techniques.

• Key figures like Norman Borlaug played a significant role in developing and promoting these agricultural innovations.

• The Green Revolution resulted in a dramatic increase in food grain production, particularly in developing countries like India and Mexico.

• Traditional Farming Techniques

• These include practices such as manual plowing, seed sowing by hand, and the use of natural fertilizers like manure.

• Traditional techniques are often labor-intensive and less efficient in terms of yield.

• They are typically more sustainable and environmentally friendly compared to modern methods that rely heavily on chemical inputs.

• Irrigation in Agriculture

• Irrigation is the artificial application of water to the soil, usually for assisting in growing crops.

• Efficient irrigation systems like drip and sprinkler irrigation can significantly enhance crop yields and water use efficiency.

• The lack of proper irrigation infrastructure was a major hurdle for farmers before the Green Revolution.

• Post-Harvest Losses

• Post-harvest losses refer to the reduction in quantity and quality of agricultural produce from the time of harvest until it reaches the consumer.

• Factors contributing to these losses include poor handling, inadequate storage facilities, and inefficient transportation systems.

• Minimizing post-harvest losses can significantly improve food security and farmer income.

questions.q: In which year did Walter Fleming stain the chromosomes to see them clearly and describe the entire process of mitosis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1882.

Key Points

• Walter Fleming, a German biologist, is renowned for his pioneering work in cell division.

• In 1882, he developed a technique to stain chromosomes, allowing them to be seen more clearly under a microscope.

• Fleming meticulously described the entire process of mitosis, coining the term "mitosis" to describe this type of cell division.

• His work laid the foundation for understanding the mechanisms of cell division and the behavior of chromosomes during this process.

Additional Information

• Chromosomes: Thread-like structures located within the nucleus of animal and plant cells that contain DNA.

• Mitosis: A type of cell division that results in two daughter cells each having the same number and kind of chromosomes as the parent nucleus.

• Staining Techniques: Methods used to enhance the contrast in samples, generally at the microscopic level, by using dyes.

• Cell Division: The process by which a parent cell divides into two or more daughter cells, crucial for growth and development in living organisms.

• Histology: The study of the microscopic structure of tissues, which was significantly advanced by Fleming's staining techniques.

questions.q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts made the president bound by the advice of the council of ministers headed by the prime minister?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 42nd.

Key Points

• The 42nd Amendment Act, also known as the "Mini-Constitution," was enacted in 1976 during the Emergency period.

• This amendment made it mandatory for the President of India to act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

• The amendment added the words "shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice" to Article 74(1) of the Indian Constitution.

• This move was aimed at reducing the discretionary powers of the President and ensuring the supremacy of the parliamentary system of government.

Additional Information

• 42nd Amendment Act

• The 42nd Amendment Act is one of the most comprehensive amendments to the Indian Constitution, making significant changes to various parts of the document.

• It attempted to reduce the independence of the judiciary and included provisions to curtail the power of the Supreme Court and High Courts.

• This amendment also added words like "Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity" to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.

• The 42nd Amendment is often criticized for its attempt to centralize power and limit the role of state governments.

• Article 74

• Article 74 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.

• Initially, the President had the discretion to reject the advice of the Council of Ministers.

• The 42nd Amendment Act removed this discretion, making the President bound to act on the advice.

• It ensures the President acts as a ceremonial head, with real executive power vested in the Council of Ministers.

• Constitutional Amendments

• Constitutional amendments are changes made to the Constitution to address emerging needs and challenges.

• They require a special majority in both Houses of Parliament and, in certain cases, ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.

• Amendments can be proposed by either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.

• Significant amendments often reflect major shifts in the country's political and social landscape.

• Emergency Period (1975-1977)

• The Emergency period in India was from 1975 to 1977, declared by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

• It involved the suspension of elections, curtailment of civil liberties, and increased centralization of power.

• The period is marked by widespread political repression and controversial constitutional changes.

• The 42nd Amendment Act is one of the key legislative changes made during this period.

questions.q: The rotating columns of air that occur over water bodies and are generally less severe than land tornadoes are known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is waterspouts.

Key Points

• Waterspouts are rotating columns of air and mist that form over a water body, commonly observed in tropical and subtropical regions.

• They are typically less intense and smaller in scale compared to tornadoes that form over land.

• Waterspouts are classified into two types: fair-weather waterspouts and tornadic waterspouts.

• Fair-weather waterspouts develop in relatively calm conditions, while tornadic waterspouts are associated with severe thunderstorms.

• Despite being less destructive, waterspouts can pose significant threats to small boats, swimmers, and coastal areas.

Additional Information

• Hurricanes

• Hurricanes are large, powerful tropical cyclones that form over warm ocean waters, primarily in the Atlantic and Northeast Pacific.

• They are characterized by strong winds, heavy rains, and can cause significant damage to coastal and inland areas.

• Hurricanes are categorized on the Saffir-Simpson scale, ranging from Category 1 (least severe) to Category 5 (most severe).

• Squalls

• Squalls are sudden, sharp increases in wind speed, often accompanied by heavy rain, thunderstorms, or snow.

• They can occur in various weather systems, including cold fronts and tropical storms.

questions.q: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court direct that, 'the Parliament cannot take away or abridge any of the fundamental rights for the Implementation of Directive Principles'?

Key Points

• The Golak Nath Case (1967) was a landmark ruling by the Supreme Court of India.

• The judgment stated that Fundamental Rights are transcendental and immutable, thus, they cannot be abridged or taken away by any amendment of the Constitution.

• The decision in Golak Nath Case was later overruled by the Kesavananda Bharati Case in 1973, which introduced the Basic Structure Doctrine.

Additional Information

• Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)

• This case is known for the Basic Structure Doctrine which asserts that certain fundamental features of the Constitution cannot be altered by any amendment.

• The judgment provided stability to the Constitution by ensuring its core values remain intact.

• Minerva Mills Case (1980)

• This case reinforced the Basic Structure Doctrine and further strengthened judicial review.

• The Supreme Court ruled that the power of judicial review is an essential feature of the Constitution.

• Indira Sawhney Case (1992)

• This case is also known as the Mandal Commission Case, which addressed the issue of reservations in government jobs.

• The Supreme Court upheld the 27% reservation for OBCs but excluded the creamy layer.

• Directive Principles of State Policy

• These are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, set out in Part IV of the Constitution.

• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.

questions.q: Which device is commonly used to connect computers within a LAN?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Switch.

Key Points

• A switch is a networking device that connects devices within a Local Area Network (LAN).

• Switches operate at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) of the OSI model, facilitating communication between connected devices.

• They use MAC addresses to forward data to the correct destination, ensuring efficient and accurate data transmission.

• Switches help in reducing network congestion by creating separate collision domains for each connected device.

• They are essential for building scalable and manageable networks, providing better performance compared to hubs.

Additional Information

• Router:

• Routers operate at the Network Layer (Layer 3) of the OSI model.

• They are used to connect multiple networks and route data packets between them.

• Routers use IP addresses to determine the best path for data transmission.

• They can provide functions such as Network Address Translation (NAT) and firewall capabilities.

• Modem:

• Modem stands for Modulator-Demodulator.

• It converts digital data from a computer into analog signals for transmission over phone lines and vice versa.

• Modems are used for connecting to the Internet via dial-up or broadband connections.

• They operate at the Physical Layer (Layer 1) of the OSI model.

• Repeater:

• Repeaters operate at the Physical Layer (Layer 1) of the OSI model.

• They are used to regenerate and amplify signals to extend the distance over which data can be transmitted.

• Repeaters do not filter or route data; they simply boost the signal strength.

• Hub:

• Hubs operate at the Physical Layer (Layer 1) of the OSI model.

• They connect multiple Ethernet devices, making them act as a single network segment.

• Hubs broadcast data to all connected devices, leading to network congestion and collisions.

• They are less efficient compared to switches and are rarely used in modern networks.

questions.q: What is the primary reason DRAM needs to be refreshed periodically?
options: To prevent data corruption caused by magnetic fields
To recharge the capacitors storing data bits
To allow the CPU to access new data
questions.solution:
The correct answer is To recharge the capacitors storing data bits.

Key Points

• Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) stores each bit of data in a separate capacitor within an integrated circuit.

• Capacitors in DRAM tend to leak charge over time, which can lead to data loss if not refreshed.

• Refreshing DRAM involves recharging the capacitors to their original state to maintain the stored data.

• This periodic refresh is necessary because capacitors in DRAM can only hold their charge for a short period, typically a few milliseconds.

• The refresh operation is managed by the memory controller, which performs the refresh cycles automatically.

Additional Information

• DRAM vs. SRAM:

• DRAM (Dynamic RAM) requires periodic refreshing to maintain data, whereas SRAM (Static RAM) does not need refreshing.

• SRAM is faster but more expensive and used for cache memory, while DRAM is cheaper and used for main memory.

• Memory Controller:

• A memory controller is a digital circuit that manages the flow of data to and from the memory.

• It is responsible for issuing refresh commands to DRAM periodically.

• Types of DRAM:

• Synchronous DRAM (SDRAM) synchronizes with the system clock for faster operation.

• Double Data Rate (DDR) SDRAM transfers data on both the rising and falling edges of the clock signal.

• Applications of DRAM:

• DRAM is widely used in computers, laptops, and smartphones as the main system memory.

• It is also used in graphics cards, gaming consoles, and other consumer electronics.

questions.q: Which type of virus infects the boot sector of floppy disks or the Master Boot Record (MBR) of hard disks?

• A Boot Sector Virus infects the boot sector of floppy disks or the Master Boot Record (MBR) of hard disks.

• These viruses are loaded into memory during the booting process of the computer, before the operating system is loaded.

• Once in memory, the virus can infect any other disk that is accessed by the system.

• Such viruses can prevent the computer from booting properly, leading to system failures and data loss.

• Historically, they were more common when floppy disks were widely used for booting computers.

Additional Information

• Direct Action Virus

• Also known as non-resident viruses.

• It attaches itself to a particular type of file (typically EXE or COM files).

• It acts immediately and infects files when executed, but does not remain in memory.

• It is easier to detect and remove compared to other types of viruses.

• Resident Virus

• Resides in a computer's RAM.

• It can infect other files and programs while they are opened or run.

• It can be harder to detect and remove since it remains active as long as the computer is on.

• Macro Virus

• Written in a macro language and typically infects documents and templates.

• Commonly associated with Microsoft Office documents.

• Activates when the infected document is opened.

• Can spread rapidly via email attachments.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about computer memory is/are correct?

1. RAM is volatile memory, meaning it loses data when power is turned off.

2. ROM is used to store essential instructions required for the computer to boot.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

Key Points

• RAM (Random Access Memory) is a type of volatile memory, meaning it loses all stored data when the power is turned off.

• RAM is used for storing data that is actively being accessed or processed by the computer’s CPU.

• ROM (Read-Only Memory) is non-volatile and retains its data even when the computer is turned off.

• ROM is used to store firmware, which is essential for the computer to boot and perform basic functions.

• Typically, the data stored in ROM is written during the manufacturing process and cannot be modified easily.

Additional Information

• Types of RAM:

• DRAM (Dynamic RAM): Needs to be refreshed thousands of times per second.

• SRAM (Static RAM): Faster and more reliable than DRAM but also more expensive.

• Types of ROM:

• PROM (Programmable ROM): Can be programmed once after manufacturing.

• EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM): Can be erased and reprogrammed using UV light.

• EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM): Can be erased and reprogrammed using electrical charge.

• Cache Memory:

• A small-sized type of volatile memory that provides high-speed data access to the CPU.

• It stores copies of frequently accessed data from the main memory.

• Virtual Memory:

• A memory management capability of an operating system that uses hardware and software to allow a computer to compensate for physical memory shortages.

• It temporarily transfers data from random access memory (RAM) to disk storage.

questions.q:
Select which of the given statement(s) is/are True or False for the Central Processing Unit (CPU) of the Computer Systems.

(i) The CPU's clock speed controls the timing and execution speed of instructions.

(ii) The CPU's cache memory provides high-speed access to frequently used instructions and data.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.

Key Points

• The CPU's clock speed indeed controls the timing and execution speed of instructions, measured in GHz (gigahertz).

• The higher the clock speed, the more instructions the CPU can process per second, resulting in better performance.

• CPU's cache memory is a small-sized type of volatile computer memory that provides high-speed data access to the processor.

• Cache memory stores copies of frequently used data from the main memory, reducing the time it takes for the CPU to access this data.

Additional Information

• CPU Cores:

• Modern CPUs come with multiple cores, allowing them to perform multiple tasks simultaneously.

• Each core can handle its own task independently of the others, which improves multitasking and overall performance.

• Hyper-Threading:

• Hyper-threading is a technology used in some CPUs to improve parallelization of computations.

• It allows a single physical core to execute multiple threads, appearing as multiple logical cores to the operating system.

• Instruction Set Architecture (ISA):

• The ISA defines the set of instructions that a CPU can execute.

• It acts as an interface between software and hardware, facilitating the execution of programs.

• Thermal Design Power (TDP):

• TDP indicates the amount of heat a CPU generates under maximum load.

• Proper cooling solutions are needed to maintain optimal CPU performance and prevent overheating.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a type of ROM that can be electronically erased and reprogrammed multiple times?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is EEPROM.

Key Points

• EEPROM stands for Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory.

• It can be erased and reprogrammed multiple times using an electrical charge.

• EEPROM is used in computers and other devices to store small amounts of data that must be saved when power is removed, such as configuration settings.

• It is non-volatile memory, meaning it retains data even when the power supply is turned off.

• EEPROMs are widely used in applications like BIOS chips, microcontrollers, smart cards, and other programmable devices.

Additional Information

• PROM (Programmable Read-Only Memory)

• PROM is a type of ROM that can be programmed once after manufacturing.

• It is used in applications where the data does not need to be changed.

• Programming PROM is done using a special device called a PROM programmer.

• EPROM (Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory)

• EPROM can be erased and reprogrammed multiple times using ultraviolet light.

• It is used in applications where data needs to be updated but not frequently.

• Erasing EPROM involves exposing it to UV light for a specified duration.

• Mask ROM

• Mask ROM is a type of ROM where data is written during the manufacturing process.

• It is used for storing firmware or data that does not require modification.

• Mask ROM is cost-effective for high-volume production but cannot be modified after manufacturing.

questions.q: What is the maximum length of characters that can be accommodated in a column in MS Excel 2003?

• Each cell can contain up to 32,767 characters, but only 255 are displayed.

• The maximum file size for an Excel 2003 workbook is 2 GB.

• Large datasets may impact performance and usability.

• Excel 2003 supports a wide range of built-in functions for mathematical, financial, and statistical calculations.

• Complex formulas can be created by combining multiple functions.
